intro: Landscape architects solve design problems, coordinate projects and analyze sites, skills that engineering and planning value. The closest of the 25 careers below is Civil Engineers, with an 85% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $100,840, which is 26% more than the $79,870 landscape architects earn.
why_it_works: Designing a site means balancing drainage, plants, codes and a client's budget, then coordinating the people who build it. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 3.88 out of 5 for this job. Civil engineering, drafting and environmental planning use the same blend of design and analysis. Most matches need no new degree. The skills to add are programming, systems analysis and technology design.
tips: Learn the design and GIS software your target field uses; technology design is one of your main gaps.
Environmental Engineers earn $107,110, which is 34% more, and value your work on water and soil.
Check whether your state lets your landscape degree count toward an engineering license.

faq.q: What jobs can former landscape architects do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Civil Engineers (85%), architectural and civil drafters (81%) and Environmental Restoration Planners (78%), based on O*NET 31.0. Interior Designers are also 73% matched, but earn $67,190, which is 16% less than the $79,870 landscape architect median.

faq.q: Which careers for landscape architects pay more?
faq.a: 8 of the 25 matches pay more. Environmental Engineers earn $107,110 (34% more), mining and geological engineers $106,220 (33% more) and Geographers $102,040 (28% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Water Resource Specialists earn $167,220 for their broader BLS group.

faq.q: Do landscape architects need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than landscape architects already have, and only 2 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is the norm, held by 86% of workers in the closest match, though engineering may need a license.

faq.q: What skills should landscape architects learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, programming, systems analysis and technology design. Coordination already rates 3.75 out of 5 for landscape architects in O*NET, so software and technical analysis are the main steps toward engineering roles.
